page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.4xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server built on x86_64 architecture using the KVM hypervisor. The instance features 16 dedicated vCPUs sourced from 8 physical Intel Xeon 8269CY cores operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. Hardware allocation includes 128 GB of RAM, yielding an 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio (8 GB per vCPU). The CPU architecture includes 35 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and hardware acceleration flags such as AVX, AVX-512F, AES, and FMA. This instance includes no bundled local SSD storage and no discrete GPU hardware, relying on external network-attached storage. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 3 Gbps.

Synthetic performance benchmarks reflect a clear distinction between single-threaded and multi-threaded workloads. Single-core tests show lower performance tiers, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 893.0 and a stress-ng single-core rating of 1108.98. However, multi-core scaling reaches average performance levels, recorded at a Geekbench multi-core score of 5757.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 13025.11. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 75.3 GB/sec, while write bandwidth registers at 53.85 GB/sec. Operational benchmarks show strong throughput for concurrent tasks, including 11.19 million Redis SET operations per second and a static web serving throughput of 7.73 GB/sec.

The hardware profile provides high memory capacity per compute unit, making ecs.se1ne.4xlarge qualitatively cost-effective for applications where memory capacity is the primary constraint rather than single-core compute speed. Tradeoffs include limited per-core instruction throughput and reliance on remote storage. Recommended workload fits include in-memory databases, Redis caching clusters, medium-scale relational database engines, static web serving, software compilation tasks, and lightweight multi-threaded data processing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.4xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server equipped with 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical Intel Xeon 8269CY cores at 2.5 GHz, along with 128 GB of RAM. Built on the KVM hypervisor, it features an 8 GB per vCPU memory allocation, 3 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and no bundled local storage or GPU hardware. Benchmark results highlight modest single-core throughput, balanced by multi-core capabilities that achieve average performance tiers in PassMark CPU tests and multi-threaded stress testing. Memory performance reaches an uncached read speed of 75.3 GB/sec, while operational benchmarks demonstrate 11.19 million Redis SET operations per second and 7.73 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Given its memory capacity relative to compute resources, ecs.se1ne.4xlarge offers strong qualitative cost efficiency for memory-heavy workloads, including in-memory key-value stores, database servers, web processing, and multi-threaded data pipelines.
